result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend two explicit modes with a separate Record button and argue well against hidden gestures. A gives more specific show-time safeguards: the paint tool is shown in the mode bar, each stroke is one undo step, and the grid frame changes in a way color-blind operators can read. It also gives a clear reason why overwriting a cue alone needs confirmation. B frankly admits that mode errors happen, but its auto-revert after one stroke would slow painting across many lights, and it wrongly says a stray paint changes all 48 lights. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend two modes plus a separate Record button and explain why hidden long-press timing is risky. B is more specific about show time: it puts the mode where the operator is looking, shows the active paint tool, makes each stroke one undo step, and asks for a named confirmation only when overwriting a cue. A is a bit more upfront about the cost of modes (forgetting which mode you're in) but overstates the risk ("changes 48 lights") and gives fewer concrete safeguards.
